meta.description: Spot-check results for Batch B (14 creators). Only entries with confidence < 85 or corrections needed.

ruleBreak.notes: Accurate. 9D Breathwork does layer 9 dimensions of sensory input on top of breathwork, turning it into a multisensory experience. Well documented on official site and multiple third-party sources.

twoWorlds.currentValue: Electronic music production and DJing meets somatic healing and breathwork. He came from the world of club culture and sound design...
twoWorlds.correctedValue: Real estate brokerage and online broadcasting meets somatic healing and breathwork. He was a successful real estate broker in his early 20s until the 2008 crisis wiped him out. After broadcasting an online radio show for 2 years, he relocated to Morocco then Bali with $360, where he co-founded a spiritual tattoo studio and discovered the power of combining breathwork with music on clients.
twoWorlds.notes: Brian Kelly's background was NOT in club culture, DJing, or sound design. He studied communication at University of San Diego, became a real estate broker, lost everything in 2008, did online radio, then moved to Bali. His music/sound approach came from the tattoo studio discovery, not a prior career in electronic music production. This is a significant factual error.

stupidSimplicity.notes: This reads like a crafted tagline rather than a verified quote from Brian Kelly. Not found in any web source. Plausible as a distillation but not verified as something he actually says.

remarkableResult.currentValue: LOW_CONFIDENCE — Built a facilitator network commonly claimed at 1,000+ across 60+ countries...
remarkableResult.correctedValue: Built a facilitator network of 2,000+ certified facilitators across 80+ countries within roughly 4-5 years (founded ~2021). Sessions use multi-layered audio combining music, binaural beats, and guided coaching to produce emotional releases in a single 45-minute session. Numbers are from 9D marketing materials (2026) and third-party coverage in Boss Magazine.
remarkableResult.notes: The original LOW_CONFIDENCE flag was appropriate but the numbers were outdated. Updated figures from 2026 sources show 2,000+ facilitators in 80+ countries, not 1,000+ in 60+. Still primarily self-reported by 9D but corroborated by Boss Magazine and other third-party coverage.

ruleBreak.notes: Accurate. Ana Forrest's approach of going INTO the pain rather than seeking bliss/transcendence is well documented. She created Forrest Yoga specifically to address trauma stored in the body.

twoWorlds.notes: Accurate. Her childhood abuse, alcoholism, bulimia, and drug addiction are documented in her memoir Fierce Medicine. Native American ceremony is confirmed as central to her practice. One minor note: sources confirm she began yoga at age 14 and was certified by 1975.

stupidSimplicity.notes: Not found as a direct quote from Ana Forrest in any web source. Plausible distillation of her philosophy but not verified as her actual words.

remarkableResult.currentValue: Built Forrest Yoga into a globally recognized style practiced across 6 continents, with hundreds of certified teachers. Her memoir 'Fierce Medicine' became a bestseller. She personally overcame epilepsy, addiction, and the effects of severe childhood trauma through the practice she created.
remarkableResult.correctedValue: Built Forrest Yoga into a globally recognized style taught in 33+ countries over 45+ years, with a network of certified Forrest Yoga teachers worldwide. Her memoir 'Fierce Medicine' was well-received (endorsed by Martha Beck) though 'bestseller' status is not independently confirmed on major bestseller lists. She personally overcame epilepsy, addiction, and the effects of severe childhood trauma through the practice she created.
remarkableResult.notes: The '6 continents' and 'hundreds of certified teachers' claims could not be verified. Web sources confirm '33+ countries' and 'certified teachers worldwide' but without specific continent or teacher counts. 'Bestseller' for Fierce Medicine is unverified on NYT or other major lists; it was well-received but the bestseller claim appears to be promotional.

ruleBreak.notes: Accurate. Dan Brulé's cross-tradition approach is well documented. He is trained in Rebirthing, Prana Yoga, Chi Kung, and multiple lineages.

twoWorlds.currentValue: Military special forces training meets spiritual healing traditions. He trained Navy SEALs, elite military units, and first responders in combat breathing, while simultaneously studying with yogic masters, Sufi teachers, and Chinese qigong practitioners.
twoWorlds.correctedValue: U.S. Navy medical deep-sea diving meets spiritual healing traditions. He served as a Navy Medical deep-sea diver during the Vietnam era (not special forces), then studied with yogic masters and qigong practitioners. He later trained Navy SEALs, elite military, first responders, and Olympic athletes in combat/performance breathing.
twoWorlds.notes: The distinction matters: Dan Brulé served as a Navy Medical deep-sea diver, not as special forces himself. He later trained SEALs and military personnel, but his own military service was as a medical diver. The current phrasing implies he was special forces, which is inaccurate. Also, 'Sufi teachers' was not confirmed in web sources; his documented training lineages are Rebirthing, Prana Yoga, and Chi Kung.

stupidSimplicity.notes: Not found as a direct quote. Plausible distillation but not verified.

remarkableResult.currentValue: Trained special forces operators, world-class martial artists, and Olympic athletes across 67+ countries over 50 years. Tony Robbins hired him as his personal breath coach. His book 'Just Breathe' became an international bestseller.
remarkableResult.correctedValue: Trained over 250,000 people across 67+ countries over 50+ years, including Navy SEALs, Olympic athletes, and corporate leaders. Tony Robbins credits Brulé's coaching with major shifts in his life (Robbins wrote the foreword to 'Just Breathe'). The book, published by Simon & Schuster, is available in 15 languages.
remarkableResult.notes: Tony Robbins is described as his coaching client and wrote the foreword, which is stronger than just 'hired him.' The book is published by Simon & Schuster in 15 languages, but 'international bestseller' status is from promotional materials, not independently confirmed on major lists. The 250,000 people figure comes from his LinkedIn and website. 'Special forces operators' should be 'Navy SEALs and military personnel' for accuracy.

ruleBreak.notes: Accurate. His sexual polarity framework that rejects both traditional patriarchy and modern gender-neutrality is well documented and is the core of his work.

twoWorlds.currentValue: Academic philosophy and biophysics research meets tantric sexuality and spiritual practice. He has a background in biophysics and academic philosophy...
twoWorlds.correctedValue: Theoretical psychobiology and neuroscience research meets tantric sexuality and spiritual practice. He graduated Phi Beta Kappa from University of Florida in Theoretical Psychobiology (combining psychology, biology, neuroscience, and computer science), then did graduate research at UC San Diego Medical School and UC Santa Cruz on nervous system evolution and immune system simulation. He departed before completing his PhD, then crossed into Tantric and Daoist sexual-spiritual traditions.
twoWorlds.notes: David Deida does NOT have a background in 'biophysics.' His degree was in Theoretical Psychobiology from University of Florida, and his graduate work was in biology at UC Santa Cruz with neuroscience research. He also did NOT study 'academic philosophy' as a field; he was a Phi Beta Kappa science graduate. This is a factual error that should be corrected.

stupidSimplicity.notes: Not found as a direct quote. Plausible distillation of his philosophy but not verified.

remarkableResult.currentValue: His book 'The Way of the Superior Man' has sold over 1 million copies and remained continuously in print since 1997... translated into 25+ languages...
remarkableResult.correctedValue: His book 'The Way of the Superior Man' has sold over 1 million copies and remained continuously in print since 1997, becoming one of the most widely read books on masculine spirituality. His eleven books collectively have been published in over 35 languages. The 20th Anniversary Edition confirms its enduring cultural impact.
remarkableResult.notes: The '25+ languages' figure appears to be understated. His publisher states his books (11 total) are published in 'over 35 languages,' though this is across all books, not necessarily just Way of the Superior Man. The 1 million copies claim is confirmed by multiple sources including Amazon and his publisher.

ruleBreak.notes: Generally accurate. His approach of simplifying breathwork to a basic two-part breath is documented, and he did strip away complexity compared to other systems.

twoWorlds.currentValue: Hollywood entertainment industry meets shamanic healing. He was working in the LA entertainment world before a personal crisis led him into healing work...
twoWorlds.correctedValue: Film/TV acting and Kentucky farm upbringing meets energy healing and breathwork. Born and raised on a farm in Kentucky, he moved to Miami in 1985 to act in commercials, then to Los Angeles in 1987 for a TV and film career. After meeting mystic healer Tim Heath, he transitioned to healing work full-time by 1997. His background in performance brought accessibility and directness to breathwork that stripped away intimidating mysticism.
twoWorlds.notes: The current description is vague ('LA entertainment world,' 'personal crisis'). The actual story is more specific: he was a working actor (commercials, TV, film) from 1985-1997, and his pivot came from meeting healer Tim Heath, not a generic 'personal crisis.' He's also from a Kentucky farm, which adds to the 'two worlds' narrative. Also, 'shamanic healing' is not how Elliott describes his work; he uses 'energy healing' and 'breathwork.'

stupidSimplicity.notes: Not found as a direct quote. His actual breath technique is described as pranayama breathing meditation, not specifically 'two breaths in, one breath out.'

remarkableResult.notes: The LOW_CONFIDENCE flag in the current data is appropriate. David Elliott is respected in the LA breathwork community and has authored books (The Reluctant Healer), teaches at Omega Institute, and created a 4-level healer training program since 2001. But specific metrics about reach, student counts, or revenue are not publicly available.

ruleBreak.correctedValue: Rejected the idea that dance parties need alcohol, darkness, and late nights. While every other dance event ran after midnight with bars, Dawnbreak created sober sunrise silent disco parties on Australian beaches at dawn, proving that the energy of a rave could be replicated at 5am without substances.
ruleBreak.notes: Dawnbreak is confirmed as a sober sunrise silent disco concept. Founded by Jian Wong Yen (co-founded with Shannon O'Connor aka DJ Shann). The concept is documented in Glam Adelaide, Humanitix event listings, and their social media. The 'rule break' of sober sunrise dancing is verifiable, but how novel it is compared to Daybreaker (founded 2013, NYC) is debatable since Daybreaker preceded them.

twoWorlds.correctedValue: Cold water swimming community building meets silent disco rave culture. Jian Wong Yen founded Cold Nips (a community ocean dip club in Western Australia) 5 years before Dawnbreak. After an accidental dance party at a Cold Nips event, he was inspired to combine the sunrise wellness ritual with silent disco technology. Co-founder Shannon O'Connor (DJ Shann) had DJed for 15 years to intoxicated crowds and wanted to play for sober audiences.
twoWorlds.notes: Jian's background is confirmed as Cold Nips founder (community ocean dipping), not a traditional DJ/music background. Shannon O'Connor brought 15 years of DJing experience. Jian's broader career background is not well documented publicly beyond the wellness/community space.

stupidSimplicity.correctedValue: Dance at sunrise, on the beach, without alcohol. That's it.
stupidSimplicity.notes: No verified tagline exists. This is a reasonable distillation based on their marketing but not a verified quote.

remarkableResult.correctedValue: In their 2026 Australian tour, drew 12,889 sunrise attendees across 10 events in 8 cities. Started in 2024 from a community dip club (Cold Nips) that had grown from 2 people to 250 regular attendees over 5 years. Co-founder DJ Shann reports 'no greater feeling than playing to thousands of sober people as the sun rises.'
remarkableResult.notes: The 12,889 attendees across 10 events in 8 cities figure comes from Glam Adelaide. Cold Nips growth (2 to 250 people) is documented in podcast interviews. Still a young company (founded 2024) so long-term results are limited.

flagged.name: Do LaB / Lightning in a Bottle

ruleBreak.notes: Accurate. LiB's integration of yoga, workshops, and art installations as co-equal with music is well documented and is their defining differentiator.

twoWorlds.currentValue: Southern California festival culture (Burning Man lineage, DIY art) meets wellness/yoga retreat programming. The Do LaB crew came from building elaborate water-based art installations at Burning Man...
twoWorlds.correctedValue: Pennsylvania-raised brothers who wanted to work in film meets Burning Man DIY art culture meets wellness/yoga retreat programming. Josh, Jesse, and Dede Flemming moved to LA wanting film careers, pivoted to throwing warehouse parties, then discovered Burning Man. At Coachella 2004, they built a 60-foot geodesic dome with a water wall that accidentally became a crowd cooling station, launching their signature water-spraying art installations. They brought this DIY festival-building energy into creating LiB as a transformational festival with structured personal development content.
twoWorlds.notes: The founders are from Pennsylvania, not Southern California natives. They wanted to be in film, not art installations. The water installations started at Coachella (2004), not at Burning Man. The current description oversimplifies their origin. Also, co-founder Dream Rockwell should be acknowledged but her departure involved controversy.

stupidSimplicity.notes: Not found as a direct quote. Plausible distillation but not verified.

remarkableResult.currentValue: Grew Lightning in a Bottle from a 300-person birthday party in 2004 to a 30,000+ attendee transformational festival, consistently selling out. Named one of the top festivals in the US by multiple outlets. Ran continuously for nearly 20 years before announcing a hiatus after 2023.
remarkableResult.correctedValue: Grew Lightning in a Bottle from a private birthday party (~100 people, 1999/2000) to an 18,000-person transformational festival by 2023, with peak years drawing up to 20,000. The first public ticketed festival (2004-2006 era) drew around 1,000-1,200 people. Named one of the top festivals in the US. The festival continues to run as of 2026 (confirmed at Buena Vista Lake) and did NOT go on hiatus after 2023.
remarkableResult.notes: Multiple errors: (1) The birthday party was ~100 people in 1999/2000, NOT 300 in 2004. (2) Peak attendance was ~18,000 (confirmed for 2023), NOT 30,000+. (3) The festival did NOT announce a hiatus after 2023; it ran in 2024, 2025, and 2026. These are significant factual errors that need correction.

ruleBreak.notes: Accurate. Her Ziva Technique combining mindfulness + meditation + manifesting into one protocol is well documented and is her differentiator from TM and mindfulness apps.

twoWorlds.currentValue: Broadway performing meets Vedic meditation. She was a Broadway actress (understudied for 'A Chorus Line' and performed in 'Chicago')...
twoWorlds.correctedValue: Broadway performing meets Vedic meditation. She was a Broadway actress for 10+ years, performing in Chicago (as Hunyak), The Producers, and A Chorus Line (2006 revival, as understudy for Val, Sheila, and Judy), as well as 42nd Street and Chitty Chitty Bang Bang. She discovered meditation to deal with insomnia, anxiety, and graying hair at age 26, then trained in Vedic meditation in India.
twoWorlds.notes: Minor inaccuracy: she didn't just 'understudy for A Chorus Line' and 'perform in Chicago.' Her IBDB credits show she performed in Chicago (as Hunyak), understudied in A Chorus Line (for Val, Sheila, Judy), The Producers, 42nd Street, and Chitty Chitty Bang Bang. She had a substantial Broadway career. The phrasing should be adjusted for accuracy.

stupidSimplicity.notes: Not found as a direct verified quote, though it aligns with her messaging.

remarkableResult.currentValue: Built Ziva Meditation into a top online meditation training, taught at Google, Harvard Business School, and Viacom. Her book 'Stress Less, Accomplish More' became a bestseller. She's trained over 20,000 students through her flagship course, and her TED talk has millions of views.
remarkableResult.correctedValue: Built Ziva Meditation into a leading online meditation training. She has spoken at Google, Harvard Business School, Apple, and Viacom (spoken at, not 'taught at'). Her book 'Stress Less, Accomplish More' debuted at #7 on Amazon and has been translated into 12 languages. She's trained 25,000-50,000+ students (numbers vary by source and time period). Named one of top 100 women in wellness.
remarkableResult.notes: Several issues: (1) She 'spoke at' Google/Harvard, she didn't 'teach at' them. (2) Student count varies: earlier sources say 15,000, more recent say 25,000 or 50,000+. The '20,000' figure is outdated. (3) The claim 'her TED talk has millions of views' is NOT verified. Her most prominent talks are an Afest talk and a Google talk, not a major TED talk. No TED talk with millions of views was found. (4) The book debuted at #7 on Amazon overall, which is impressive but different from being a NYT bestseller.

ruleBreak.notes: Accurate. The jungle-as-venue concept and structural commitment to permaculture/sustainability are well documented.

twoWorlds.currentValue: Central American eco-village/permaculture movement meets electronic music festival culture. Founded by people embedded in the Costa Rica intentional community scene...
twoWorlds.correctedValue: American ethnobotany and tropical permaculture meets electronic music festival culture. Co-founded by Stephen Brooks (Miami-born, lifelong Deadhead and Burning Man attendee, self-trained ethnobotanist) and Sarah Wu. Brooks had been living in Costa Rica since 1995 running the Punta Mona Center for Regenerative Design and had taught 40+ Permaculture Design Courses. He brought deep roots in the regenerative community, not just 'the Costa Rica intentional community scene.'
twoWorlds.notes: The current description is vague. Stephen Brooks is specifically identified as the co-founder, and he's American (Miami-born), not a generic 'person embedded in the Costa Rica scene.' He is a self-trained ethnobotanist and the founder of Punta Mona, a world-leading tropical permaculture center. Sarah Wu is co-founder. This is more specific and accurate.

stupidSimplicity.notes: Not found as a direct quote. Plausible distillation but not verified.

remarkableResult.currentValue: Grew from a scrappy jungle gathering in 2011 to a 5,000-6,000 person annual festival in Uvita, Costa Rica that sells out and draws an international audience...
remarkableResult.correctedValue: Grew from its first edition in 2011 in Dominical to a 5,000-10,000 person annual festival in Uvita, Costa Rica (some sources cite up to 10,000 attendees). Became a flagship example of the 'transformational festival' category. Based on 8 core tenets including permaculture, spirituality, movement, art, music, community, health, and eco-building.
remarkableResult.notes: Attendance estimates vary: some sources say 5,000+, others say nearly 10,000. The range should be acknowledged. The first festival was in Dominical, then moved to nearby Uvita. Otherwise the description is reasonably accurate.

ruleBreak.notes: Accurate. Her repackaging of Kundalini yoga with modern aesthetics for LA's creative class is well documented by Newsweek, LAist, Vice, and LAmag.

twoWorlds.notes: Accurate. Celebrity followers confirmed (Kate Hudson, Alicia Keys, Orlando Bloom, Russell Brand). Her deep embedding in both traditional Kundalini (Yogi Bhajan lineage) and LA celebrity/fashion culture is well documented.

stupidSimplicity.notes: Not found as a direct verified quote. Plausible distillation of her approach but not verified.

remarkableResult.currentValue: Built RA MA Institute into one of the most high-profile yoga studios in LA, with locations in Venice and Mallorca. Celebrity following included artists and musicians. Died unexpectedly in 2021 at age 41...
remarkableResult.correctedValue: Built RA MA Institute into one of the most high-profile yoga studios in LA, with locations in Venice, New York, Mallorca, and Boulder (described as founder of '7 global businesses'). Celebrity following included Kate Hudson, Alicia Keys, Orlando Bloom, and Russell Brand. Died of pulmonary embolism after ankle surgery on August 1, 2021 at age 41. Her legacy is complicated by QAnon conspiracy theory promotion, Yogi Bhajan lineage abuse allegations, and former employee accusations of cult-like dynamics at RA MA.
remarkableResult.notes: Minor additions: (1) RA MA had locations beyond Venice and Mallorca (also NYC, Boulder). (2) Death cause was pulmonary embolism after ankle surgery, worth noting. (3) Celebrity names should be specified as they are well-documented. (4) The QAnon controversy is well-documented by NPR, LAist, and Vice and should be explicitly named rather than just 'reports of cult-like dynamics.'

passed.name: Bikram Choudhury
passed.notes: All facts well-verified. 26 postures, 105F room, 1,650 studios by 2006, franchise model, sexual assault allegations, Netflix documentary, fleeing the US. The only minor quibble is stupidSimplicity being unverifiable as a direct quote, but the content accurately reflects his philosophy.

passed.name: Dan Hughes
passed.notes: All facts well-verified. DDP, PACE model (Playfulness, Acceptance, Curiosity, Empathy), foster care focus, UK adoption by child welfare systems, books with Jonathan Baylin confirmed. DDP is recognized as evidence-based. stupidSimplicity is a reasonable distillation but not a verified direct quote.

passed.name: DJ Taz Rashid
passed.notes: Most facts verified. Born in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Corporate jobs in hotels, real estate, university recruiting (not just 'corporate recruiter'). Laid off in 2011 (confirmed). Plays guitar, keyboard, Native American flute, didgeridoo, hand percussion (confirmed). 700 newsletter signups at one event (confirmed by YogaJournal interview). The remarkableResult LOW_CONFIDENCE flag is appropriately cautious. stupidSimplicity is unverifiable as a quote. Overall accurate enough to pass.

passed.name: Gabby Reece
passed.notes: All facts well-verified. Pro volleyball career confirmed. XPT co-created with Laird Hamilton. Podcast 'The Gabby Reece Show' confirmed (ranked #1 in mental health category per one source). Co-founded Laird Superfood (publicly traded). Nike's first female signature athlete. Three-decade relevance span confirmed. stupidSimplicity is a reasonable distillation but not a verified direct quote.
